title: veafGroundAI marker commands run with no security check
outcome_detail: Fixed structurally rather than per-instance. veafCommands.registerCommandHandler now takes a required security argument and asserts on a missing or unknown one, and the dispatcher enforces it centrally; veafSpawn.registerCommandHandler lost its documented 'legacy 2-arg form = no check'. The inventory the ticket asked for found VMR-003 was one of FOUR ungated handlers: veafGroundAI (reported), plus veafMove, veafNamedPoints and the veafRadio marker path (not reported). Levels set by David 2026-08-06: veafGroundAI L9, veafMove L1, veafRadio L1, veafNamedPoints OPEN. Changes existing missions -- three commands anyone could use now need a pilot level or a login.

outcome_detail: veafRadio._transmitViaSRS now strips shell metacharacters from the free-text values (message, station name, file path) and validates the small-shape ones (frequencies, modulations, coalition) against an anchored pattern, falling back with a warning. Reachability was confirmed while fixing: markTextAnalysis reads an F10 marker and nothing on that path authenticates, so any player reached os.execute on the server host. Six tests in test_veafRadio.lua; five of them fail without the fix. Security half closed by ticket 03: the veafRadio marker path now declares L1 and the dispatcher enforces it, so the shell-safety fix is no longer the only thing between a spectator and os.execute.

title: dcs-fiddle-server executes arbitrary Lua from unauthenticated HTTP requests
outcome_detail: ADR 0019. The port stays open for now because no DCS is available to test a change to the transport FEAT-DCS-SMOKE-HARNESS speaks through, and shipping untested auth there breaks the harness invisibly. Two things did ship: the harness documentation now carries a danger warning where it tells you to install the hook, and the token design is written down to be implemented with the harness's remaining slice, where it can be tested. Severity is understated in the review: cors='*' plus a GET channel means any web page visited while the hook is installed gets code execution, so 'loopback only' is not the protection it sounds like.

title: onEvent aborts all remaining match managers on a coalition mismatch

tonumber(nil) comparison crashes on valueless size/defense/armor/spacing marker keywords
outcome_detail: Ticket 06 group A / PR #677 — the four valueless numeric keywords (size, defense, armor, spacing) each crashed twice: string.format('%d', nil) and tonumber(nil) <= 5. Both go through veaf.safeNumber now. The review asked for this in 'the shared marker parser'; there is none — ten modules carry their own markTextAnalysis — so the shared piece is the conversion, which is what was being written wrong each time. Out-of-range values stay ignored rather than clamped, preserving existing behaviour.
